items.title: Nvidia stock falls amid probe into CEO’s relationship with Chinese spy
items.summary:
By Steve Kopack and Rob Wile

Nvidia’s stock slid about 4% on Monday after the company announced that it had opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman that U.S. intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy.

The probe has the potential to unsettle the entire AI boom, fueled by trillions of dollars of spending and investments, in part to purchase Nvidia’s cutting-edge AI chips. Nvidia’s drop wiped out more than $200 billion in value. [...] Nvidia’s peers, such as AMD, Qualcomm, Taiwan Semi and Intel, all rose along with the broader market. Nvidia was the biggest loser on the Dow, the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500.

With so many outstanding questions about the Huang scandal, few major analysts that cover Nvidia had weighed in on Monday morning about what it could mean for the company’s future.

But those who did said it was a blemish on an otherwise sterling track record, which could spark even more investigations. [...] “A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation,” Nvidia said in a Sunday statement. “The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.”

An Nvidia spokesperson told NBC News that Huang was “committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption.”

The massive artificial intelligence chip maker Nvidia says it is launching an internal investigation, after reports that the company's CEO was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. The company started as a manufacturer of chips for computer graphics, which later turned out to be crucial for training artificial intelligence.

Nvidia's CEO and President Trump have repeatedly appeared in public together in recent years. According to Huang, Nvidia is helping to fund the construction of a new ballroom at the White House. [...] In the statement announcing the investigation, Nvidia cited recent reporting by The New York Times, which alleges Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation that sought to send advanced Nvidia AI chips to China.

"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the statement from the company's board of directors reads in part.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits affair, board to launch investigation
items.summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy in a message to his company, and the company's board announced an independent investigation Sunday.

Why it matters:The scandal raises national security concerns involving one of the world's most powerful tech CEOs, who has pushed to loosen restrictions on selling advanced AI chips to China amid the two countries' race for technological dominance. [...] "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did."
   Huang said he took "full responsibility" for his actions, adding that he had fallen short of his responsibilities to Nvidia's employees, board and shareholders.
   "Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life," Huang wrote. "I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence." [...] Driving the news: "I owe my family and all of you an apology," Huang wrote in a draft email to Nvidia employees obtained by Axios.

items.title: Jensen Huang's affair highlights Nvidia's key man risk with no heir
items.summary:
Nvidia has long maintained a flat, non-hierarchical organizational structure. Huang has deep involvement in the company's day-to-day operations and frequently serves as its spokesperson in front of world leaders and at industry conferences. In addition to being co-founder and CEO, Huang is also Nvidia's president. [...] Nvidia's board "needs to demonstrate independence and protect shareholders without destabilizing a company whose success is unusually dependent on its founder," Schulze-Melander wrote. "Its initial statement suggests it is attempting to achieve both."

Several analysts said the investigation could lead to governance changes at Nvidia, including putting a transition contingency plan in place. [...] The Melius analysts wrote that Nvidia has a "strong bench" of executive talent across its networking, hyperscale and high-performance computing businesses, along with "technical expertise" stemming from Chief Technology Officer Michael Kagan as well as Dally, the chief scientist.

"While these folks can keep the engine running, Jensen is one of a kind, and his energy will be needed to maintain confidence in the AI trade," the analysts wrote.

items.title: Bun creator Jarred Sumner rewrote a million lines of code with Claude in 11 days, and every line was checked by two agen
items.summary:
Bun creator Jarred Sumner rewrote a million lines of code with Claude in 11 days, and every line was checked by two agents that didn't write it

I broke down his setup, added one more layer of control on top, and packed it all into one prompt for Opus 5.5

→ one agent writes the code
→ two others, each in its own context, see only the diff and have to prove it doesn't work
→ a fourth agent checks the checkers, drops false alarms and looks for what they missed
→ whoever writes doesn't review, and whoever reviews doesn't write
→ reviewers reject stubs, weakened tests and "explanatory" comments instead of real fixes
→ if a bug repeats, the agent doesn't patch the code, it adds a rule so it never happens again
→ it's done only when every test passes and none are skipped

Throw it at Opus 5.5 with the task you're scared to hand to an agent, and see how many bugs it catches on its own.

The full prompt is in the comments.

How to tune it for your own work is in the article below. Save it before it gets lost ↓

items.title: SNAPRAG: Cost-Efficient Knowledge Extraction Attack on RAG Systems via Adversarial Perturbations
items.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems improve Large Language Model (LLM) responses by incorporating information from external knowledge bases. However, recent studies have shown that attackers can extract substantial portions of private knowledge bases from RAG systems through repeated querying. Yet, state-of-the-art extraction attacks either rely heavily on external LLMs to generate adversarial queries or require a large number of queries. In this paper, we propose SNAPRAG, a novel and cost-efficient attack for extracting RAG knowledge bases through adversarial perturbations. Our approach algorithmically generates adversarial queries without relying on external LLMs and allows for a strictly configurable query budget. In particular, SNAPRAG uses a discrete token-mutation algorithm to generate novel queries in a strict black-box setting. Our adaptive dissimilarity threshold calibration systematically forces queries into unexplored semantic regions of the target database, enabling extraction with fewer queries. Specifically, to extract half of the target knowledge base, our method requires up to 6.77$\times$ fewer queries than existing approaches. Furthermore, within a fixed query budget, our method recovers up to 96.9%, outperforming the closest approach by 7.7-19.9%. We further evaluate SNAPRAG against active defenses, where it remains the leading attack on four of five defended targets, achieving 50.7-96.3% extraction rate.

items.title: Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for ICU Discharge Risk Assessment
items.summary: Unplanned 30-day intensive care unit (ICU) readmission is a critical benchmark for evaluating healthcare quality. Most predictive models assume readmission risk depends solely on a patient's individual pathophysiological state, ignoring hospital operational context and resource capacity. In practice, discharge decisions are dynamic trade-offs between patient stability and bed turnover pressures. To address this gap, we develop an Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for ICU discharge risk assessment. The system combines multi-agent collaborative extraction with self-evolving retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to eliminate template noise from progress notes, while constructing departmental workload indicators alongside admission flow features, continuous vital signs, and sparse medical codes (ICD/DRG). Addressing severe class imbalance (about 10.5% readmissions) and alarm fatigue, we implement data normalization, class reweighting, and decision-threshold calibration. In 20 independent runs across 20,000 ICU stays from MIMIC-III, empirical findings demonstrate that: vital signs alone have limited predictive capacity under real-world class imbalance (PR-AUC of 0.1387 +/- 0.0086); directly concatenating raw text embeddings degrades decision tree performance (XGBoost and LightGBM PR-AUC drop to 0.3893 and 0.4030); whereas an end-to-end multimodal fine-tuning architecture (Transformer E2E FineTune) utilizing layer-wise parameter freezing and differential learning rates reverses text negative transfer, achieving the highest AUROC of 0.8288 +/- 0.0110, PR-AUC of 0.4373 +/- 0.0310, and F1-Score of 0.4757 +/- 0.0196. Operational indicators supply independent risk signals, laying an engineering foundation for high-utility clinical decision support tools.

items.title: AOP-Smart-Finder: A High-Throughput Human-AI Hybrid Framework for AOP Discovery and Evidence Mapping from Large-Scale Literature
items.summary: The rapid growth of scientific literature and the high heterogeneity of biological terminology and mechanistic descriptions make it difficult for researchers to integrate scattered research evidence, identify connections among biological events, and construct mechanistic networks. Here, we developed a high-throughput human-AI hybrid framework, AOP-Smart-Finder, for biological event discovery, relationship mining, and Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) construction and evidence mapping from large-scale literature. This framework integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), AOP-Smart retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology, and Python-based automation, supporting two analysis modes: one based on a single compound and the other based on a predefined set of biological events. In the di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) case, the system processed 12,983 articles within 30 min and included 1,093 of them, from which it extracted 1,589 biological events (including 458 official key events [KEs] and 1,131 candidate KEs) and 2,519 key event relationships (KERs). In the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) case, the system identified 55 stressors from 437 articles and extracted 278 biological events and 548 event relationships. Following manual curation and Weight of Evidence (WoE) evaluation, a mechanistic network comprising 16 KEs and 23 KERs was ultimately constructed. This framework can either use existing AOPs as knowledge guidance for mechanistic expansion and evidence supplementation, or discover novel event connections and construct mechanistic networks around user-specified research topics. It provides a high-throughput, traceable, human-AI hybrid methodology for complex biological mechanism elucidation and AOP discovery driven by large-scale literature.
